numbers.value: “Figure out where in the past the subject is currently living.”
numbers.label: Search manual, dementia chapter
numbers.source_name: Robert Koester, Lost Person Behavior — Dementia
numbers.quote: Figure out where in the past the subject is currently “living” in order to determine possible destinations (e.g., a former residence, a work place).

numbers.value: “List locations even if they no longer exist.”
numbers.label: Search manual questionnaire
numbers.source_name: Robert Koester, Lost Person Behavior — Dementia
numbers.quote: List all of the subject’s addresses, dwelling types, and how long he has lived at each address going back to childhood. List locations even if they no longer exist.

numbers.label: UK Herbert Protocol is named after a veteran who died looking for his childhood home
numbers.source_name: Police Scotland
numbers.quote: It originated in Norfolk and takes its name after Normandy landings veteran George Herbert, who lived with dementia and died in 2011, after going missing whilst looking for his childhood home.

numbers.value: “Any important past addresses including childhood addresses or past jobs.”
numbers.label: Herbert Protocol form field
numbers.source_name: Thames Valley Police — Herbert Protocol form
numbers.quote: Any important past addresses including childhood addresses or past jobs.

numbers.label: recent memories are lost before older ones
numbers.source_name: Wixted, Psychological Review 111(4) 2004
numbers.quote: T. Ribot's (1881) law of retrograde amnesia states that brain damage impairs recently formed memories to a greater extent than older memories

numbers.label: of 325 US missing-dementia news reports: said they were trying to reach a former residence, workplace or a relative's home
numbers.source_name: Rowe et al., BMC Geriatrics 11:28 (2011)
numbers.quote: A small percentage of individuals (8%) indicated they were trying to get to a former residence or work location or a relative's home.

numbers.label: were on a usual, permitted errand alone just before going missing (325 US cases)
numbers.source_name: Rowe et al., BMC Geriatrics 11:28 (2011)
numbers.quote: The majority of individuals (58%) were engaged in an appropriate and permitted unsupervised activity just prior to the missing incident.

numbers.label: Deaths happened mostly in unpopulated areas (exposure, drowning), closer to where they were last seen
numbers.source_name: Rowe et al., BMC Geriatrics 11:28 (2011)
numbers.quote: Deaths most commonly occurred in unpopulated areas due to exposure and drowning. Those who died were found closer to the place last seen and took longer to find

numbers.label: UK police scheme that records routines and known locations in advance (online Herbert Protocol, plus optional tags): first missing incidents after joining were found in 2.73 h vs 5.39 h before (846 people)
numbers.period: Avon and Somerset Police data to June 2023 (published 2026)
numbers.source_name: Morrissey, King, Au-Yeung, Hornberger — Innovation in Aging 10(3) igaf132 (2026)
numbers.quote: Individuals with first missing incidents occurring after joining the scheme were found significantly faster (2.73 hours) than those with a first incident occurring before joining the scheme (5.39 hours).

numbers.label: of lost Alzheimer's subjects were found in a creek or drainage and/or caught in briars or bushes
numbers.source_name: Koester, Lost Alzheimer's subject behavioral profile (dbs-sar.com), from Koester & Stooksbury, Wilderness and Environmental Medicine 6:34-43 (1995)
numbers.quote: Subject usually found in a creek, or drainage and/or caught in briars/bushes (63%)

numbers.label: Search records: of the found-in-a-house cases, half traveled to a previous residence; the one found after a long delay was in an uninhabited former residence
numbers.source_name: Koester & Stooksbury, Wilderness and Environmental Medicine 6:34-43 (1995)
numbers.quote: In the 4 cases in which patients were in a house, 2 were hiding in their own house and 2 traveled to a previous residence.

numbers.value: “Small details like that are key clues.”
numbers.label: Korean missing-person investigator: families should note what the person often says and does; a woman found near Sinchon had lived there when young
numbers.source_name: Hankyoreh, Eunpyeong Police missing-person team, 2019-05-29
numbers.quote: 가족들이 평소 치매노인이 자주 하던 말이나 행동 등을 유심히 봐두었다가 신고 뒤 경찰에 알려주면 수사에 큰 도움이 된다 … 젊었을 때 그 근처에서 살았다고 하더라고요. 그런 사소한 정보 하나하나가 수사에 매우 중요한 단서가 됩니다.
